items.canonical_answer: Paid communication intended to inform or influence potential buyers about a product or organisation.
marking_guidance: Meaning/definition and essential element (1): paid communication with an informing/influencing purpose towards potential buyers.

items.prompt: Identify two features establishing an invented workshop’s paid opening notice as advertising.
items.canonical_answer: It is paid communication; it aims to inform potential buyers about the workshop’s service.
marking_guidance: Characteristic (1): paid communication. Distinction/example (1): informing potential buyers about a service.

items.prompt: Explain how a clear opening-hours poster on a permitted noticeboard can serve an informative advertising purpose when the intended local customers regularly pass it.
items.canonical_answer: The poster communicates when the service is available. Regular passers-by encounter the information, making it easier for interested households to plan a visit. Awareness can support a purchase but does not guarantee one.
marking_guidance: Starting change (1): opening-hours message displayed. Because/mechanism (1): intended customers regularly encounter it. Link (1): availability information reduces difficulty planning a visit. Consequence (1): awareness can support consideration without guaranteeing purchase. Total 4.

items.prompt: Explain the advertising purpose of an invented repairer’s paid message stating its service location and Saturday opening hours.
items.canonical_answer: It informs potential buyers where and when the service is available, helping them identify an opportunity to use it.
marking_guidance: Context (1): location/opening facts. Reason/conclusion (1): information helps potential buyers find and consider the service.

items.prompt: Define advertising (2). Identify the purpose of each original message: “Open Saturday, 08:00–12:00” and “Choose the convenience of your local repair desk” (2). Explain one purpose of repeating an opening notice (2). Identify two advertising methods that can carry a message to potential customers (2).
items.canonical_answer: Advertising is paid communication intended to inform or influence potential buyers. The opening-hours message is informative; the convenience message is persuasive. Repetition can remind people of the service, keeping it in attention before they decide. Posters and radio announcements are possible methods.
marking_guidance: Meaning (2): paid communication (1), informing/influencing potential buyers (1). Separate points for purposes (2): informative (1), persuasive (1). Explanation (2): reminder purpose (1), keeps service in attention before a decision (1). Methods (2): poster (1), radio (1). Marks allocation 8.

items.prompt: Invented Namibian case: Blue Pebble Repairs has N$200 for a paid local notice about its new bicycle-service desk. Intended customers regularly pass a community noticeboard where advertising is permitted. The message states its location and Saturday opening hours and adds “Choose convenient local service”. Describe three features of the advertising (6). Explain its informative purpose (4). Explain how the noticeboard method fits the stated audience and resources without guaranteeing purchases (4).
items.canonical_answer: It is paid communication, it supplies opening/location facts and it includes a persuasive convenience message. Information helps interested households find the desk and plan a visit. The permitted board is encountered by the intended local customers and a small notice fits the stated budget, connecting the method to the audience. A household still needs to want and afford the service, so awareness is not a guaranteed purchase.
marking_guidance: Context/data description (6): paid notice (1), N$200 resource stated (1); factual content (1), location/hours supplied (1); persuasive element (1), convenience phrase supplied (1). Mechanism/explanation part 1 (4): conveys availability (1), tells location (1), reduces search difficulty (1), helps plan a visit (1). Explanation part 2 (4): intended customers pass board (1), paid display permitted (1), small notice fits stated resources (1), awareness still requires willingness/ability before purchase (1). Marks allocation 6+4+4=14.
